classification: SYNTHETIC NONPROD FIXTURE DATA. A fictional Taylor operating company invented for nonprod acceptance. NOT historical Taylor data, NOT production, NOT the Certification world, and NOT real people, customers, addresses, phone numbers or equipment.

supersedes.note: Every v1 Employee, Principal, Account, Contact, Location and Commercial record id/number is carried forward BYTE-IDENTICAL so v2 extends the same world rather than creating a second one. v2 adds profile facts, reporting relationships, a third Account, more Contacts/Locations/Commercial records, and the operational domains.

rulings.jobRole: Job Role authority is NOT YET IMPLEMENTED in PostgreSQL (EMP-RT-08). Every jobRole value here is seed-manifest metadata only. No seed step writes it to any PostgreSQL authority column, and a test asserts that.
rulings.jobRoleIsNotSecurityRole: Job Role and Security Role are independent. No Security Role is derived from a Job Role and no Job Role is derived from a Security Role. Both are declared explicitly, per persona.
rulings.salesJobRoles: Retail Sales and National Accounts Sales are SEPARATE Job Roles. A generic Job Role named SALES is forbidden and refused by the manifest validator.
rulings.identityChain: Credential -> Principal -> governed tenant membership -> governed Employee/Principal link -> Employee. A Firebase uid is never an Employee id. Employee != User Access. Credential != Principal != Employee.
rulings.principals: Seeded Principals use the identity provider `eos-synthetic-nonprod`, which NO authentication verifier recognizes, so they can never sign in. They exist to exercise governed Principal / membership / Role-assignment / Employee-link relationships. The ONE real administrator Principal is REUSED, never recreated and never re-credentialed.
rulings.responsibility: Record Owner, Accountable Person and Assigned Person are three distinct facts and are never collapsed. Ownership is owner_employee_id; accountability is the governed establishment + mint; assignment has no PostgreSQL authority in any domain this manifest touches and is therefore never written.
rulings.accountability: GOVERNED/SEED: accountable_employee_id is persisted only from the value the governed establishment + mint produced, in the same transaction as the record, and only while it is still NULL. This is not live write activation and does not close activation blocker #2.
rulings.catalogWriterState: functions/src/catalogMaster/catalogWriterState.ts declares CATALOG_WRITER_AUTHORITY = { firestore: OPEN, postgres: INACTIVE }. This seed therefore NEVER invokes postgresPartMasterWriter or postgresEquipmentModelWriter. Part DESCRIPTIVE facts stay manifest metadata; only the Part IDENTITY row (eos_ops.parts) is seeded.
rulings.firebase: Firebase is transitional credential entry only. This seed opens no Firebase connection, creates no Firestore document, and declares no Firebase business authority.
rulings.runtimeIdentityProvider: THE RUNTIME PROVIDER IS `firebase`, MEASURED NOT GUESSED. functions/src/eosApi/server.ts:101 reads `identityProvider: (env.EOS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER ?? "firebase").trim()`; :111-124 createFirebaseTokenVerifier returns `{ externalSubject: decoded.uid, identityProvider }` and reads ONLY the uid, never a custom claim; that pair goes straight into resolveOperationalContext -> resolvePrincipalContext, which looks the Principal up by (identity_provider, external_subject). render.yaml's eos-api-nonprod service does NOT set EOS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER, so the default `firebase` applies, and its GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is eos-platform-sandbox. functions/src/adminPolicy/principalContext.ts:38 declares FIREBASE_IDENTITY_PROVIDER = "firebase".
rulings.firebaseIsIdentityOnly: Firebase Auth is TRANSITIONAL IDENTITY AND SESSION ONLY. It is never Employee authority, Security Role authority, capability authority, profile authority, ownership authority, workflow authority or any other business persistence. A Firebase uid is ONLY a Principal's external subject and is NEVER an Employee id. The Sample Company credential path uses firebase-admin/auth and is structurally forbidden from importing firebase-admin/firestore.

company.syntheticAddressPolicy: Every street address is on a fictional street in the fictional city of Sampleton, state ZZ, postal code 00000. Every telephone number is in the NANP fiction-reserved 555-01XX range. None of these resolve to a real place or a real line.
company.$comment: operatingCompanyKey is deliberately DISTINCT from any real Taylor operating company key. eos_ops rows this seed writes are therefore confined to a company nothing else in nonprod uses.

3. ... --mode activate-logins --apply --firebaseProjectId ...  -- sandbox Auth accounts (passwordless), firebase Principals, atomic link transition

userAccess.reason: ON_LEAVE. Application access was removed for the duration of the leave. The Employee record, the employment history and the reporting relationship all remain; the person simply has no Principal and no credential. This is the Employee != User Access proof for a non-ACTIVE lifecycle status.

THE EMPLOYEE != USER ACCESS PROOF. An ACTIVE, fully-profiled, managed Employee who has never had, and does not need, any application access: no Principal, no tenant membership, no Security Role, no credential. A verifier that reports this person as 'missing access' has confused the two concepts.

principals.$comment: The ONE real administrator Principal in the nonprod tenant. REUSED verbatim: never recreated, never renamed, never re-credentialed, and its Role set is left exactly as v1 left it.

loginPrincipal.$comment: The ONE real sandbox Administrator Principal. Reused exactly as it is: never recreated, never re-subjected, its credential never rotated, its Role set never changed. It is linked to the Sample Owner/Executive Employee, and its visible person name comes from that Employee's display name through the governed Employee record -- never from its raw external subject.

expectedAccess.$contract: Per login-capable persona: requiredCapabilities MUST all resolve through Credential -> Principal -> membership -> Role assignments -> role_capabilities -> effective set; forbiddenCapabilities MUST NOT. The verifier resolves the EFFECTIVE set with functions/src/eosOps/capabilityAuthority.ts capabilitiesForRoleKeys and never accepts the existence of an assignment row as proof.
expectedAccess.$postgresCapabilityVocabulary_comment: THE GOVERNED POSTGRESQL CAPABILITY VOCABULARY, in full. eos_policy.capabilities is registered by migration, not by the in-repo Role catalog, and it currently holds these 43 ids and no others -- the two newest being workOrder.create and workOrder.transition, added by migration 1761264000000 for the native Work Order authority (workOrder.cancel is deliberately NOT among them: workOrder.lifecycle.cancel already means it) -- while PERMISSION_CATALOG holds several hundred. Every requiredCapabilities / forbiddenCapabilities id above is drawn from THIS list, because a capability the PostgreSQL authority does not know cannot be granted, cannot be resolved, and therefore cannot be proved either way. Role-catalog ids outside it are reported as CAPABILITY_VOCABULARY_PARTIAL rather than silently expected. The verifier asserts this list equals the live table, so a vocabulary migration is a reviewed change here.

expectedAccess.$gapClassification_comment: EVERY access finding carries EXACTLY ONE of the five governed classes. The class decides what may be done about it, which is why a vague 'gap' is not allowed to exist here: SEED_GRANT_GAP = the capability IS registered in eos_policy.capabilities and the Role catalog DOES declare it for this Role, but the live role_capabilities row is missing -- the governed reconciliation may add it. POSTGRES_VOCABULARY_GAP = a legitimate, currently-governed PostgreSQL runtime operation whose capability is a governed platform capability, but eos_policy.capabilities has no registration -- NEVER auto-fixed here; the exact capability and authority evidence are returned and a registration migration is PROPOSED separately, never authored. DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER = the function is still legacy/non-PostgreSQL, so the scenario stays BLOCKED and NO PostgreSQL capability is invented for it. NOT_A_GAP = the model is already correct and nothing should change. CONDITIONAL_AUTHORITY_GAP = role_capabilities cannot honestly encode the intended condition or scope. A Role is NEVER widened globally to make one persona scenario pass.

accessFindings.finding: Retail Sales and National Accounts Sales are SEPARATE Job Roles and both hold the single `salesperson` Security Role.
accessFindings.whyNotADefect: Their APPLICATION PERMISSIONS are intentionally identical -- both own Accounts, run a pipeline, draft and accept agreements and raise Sales Orders. Job Role and Security Role are independent axes, and mirroring the Job Role vocabulary into the Security Role catalog would assert a permission difference that does not exist and would couple the two axes the rulings keep apart. The two populations are distinguished where the difference is real: Job Role, Account segment, record ownership and the reporting line.
accessFindings.action: NONE. No Security Role is created. Previously reported as NATIONAL_ACCOUNTS_SALES_HAS_NO_DISTINCT_SECURITY_ROLE, which was the wrong framing.

accessFindings.finding: The `technician` Role's eight permissions are workOrder.transition plus seven reorder.* ids. None is registered in eos_policy.capabilities, so a technician resolves to an EMPTY effective PostgreSQL capability set.
accessFindings.authorityEvidence: Work Orders have no table in functions/migrations at all and the Reorder runtime is the Firestore command path; neither function has been cut over to PostgreSQL, so there is no governed PostgreSQL operation for these ids to authorize.
accessFindings.action: BLOCKED. No PostgreSQL capability is invented and no Role is widened. The technician contract declares no required capability and proves the denials only. Completes when the Work Order and Reorder domains cut over.

accessFindings.finding: fieldManager/dispatcher/officeManager declare workOrder.create / .transition / .cancel, none of which is registered. eos_policy.capabilities separately registers workOrder.lifecycle.dispatch / .complete / .cancel, which NO Role in the catalog declares. The two halves have never met.
accessFindings.authorityEvidence: No work order table exists in functions/migrations; the Work Order runtime remains Firestore-authoritative. The registered workOrder.lifecycle.* ids anticipate a cutover that has not happened.
accessFindings.action: BLOCKED. Scenario D stays BLOCKED. The Owner/Executive contract FORBIDS workOrder.lifecycle.dispatch so that nobody can quietly start resolving it, and no Role is granted it.

accessFindings.finding: No reorder.* capability id is registered in eos_policy.capabilities.
accessFindings.authorityEvidence: The eos_ops purchasing repository is a governed PostgreSQL WRITER, but nothing resolves a purchasing capability at request time: functions/src/eosOps/eosOpsHttp.ts:176 serves exactly one route, /operations/inventory, and its operation set is READ-only. The purchasing RUNTIME is still the Firestore command path, so there is no governed PostgreSQL operation for a reorder.* capability to authorize. This is deliberately NOT classified POSTGRES_VOCABULARY_GAP: registering a capability no PostgreSQL runtime checks would be inventing authority.
accessFindings.action: BLOCKED. Purchasing RECORDS are seeded through the governed repository; purchasing CAPABILITIES are not granted or asserted.

accessFindings.finding: inventory.location.bin.manage, inventory.location.bin.read, inventory.balance.read and warehouse.transferOrder.read are declared by Roles but are not registered in eos_policy.capabilities.
accessFindings.authorityEvidence: Same evidence as above: the warehouse/bin and transfer repositories are governed PostgreSQL writers with no request-time PostgreSQL authorization path. The bins themselves ARE seeded through the governed repository.
accessFindings.action: BLOCKED. No capability invented. Cycle-count capabilities, which ARE registered and DO have a governed PostgreSQL path, are asserted normally and resolve.

accessFindings.finding: The reorder execution ids a Parts Associate would need (startPurchasing, recordPurchaseOrder, markReceived) live on the `technician` compatibility Role under an operationalRoleActive(PARTS_ASSOCIATE) CONDITION.
accessFindings.authorityEvidence: eos_policy.role_capabilities carries a (role, capability) pair and NO condition column, so the condition cannot be represented. Assigning `technician` to a Parts Associate to obtain them would grant them UNCONDITIONALLY -- precisely the defect R-32 removed from that Role.
accessFindings.action: BLOCKED. partsAssociate + inventoryReceivingClerk are assigned instead. The Role is NOT widened and `technician` is NOT assigned to a non-technician.

seedGrantGap.finding: Every (Role, capability) pair the Role catalog declares for a Sample Company Role whose capability IS registered in eos_policy.capabilities but whose live role_capabilities row is missing.
seedGrantGap.action: RECONCILED through the existing governed mechanism only (eosOps/migration/inventoryCapabilityGrantMigration.ts): dry run first, tenant-scoped, insert-missing-only, idempotent, unresolved Role or unknown capability refuses the run, no ad-hoc SQL, never a pair the Role catalog does not declare for that Role, and no new Security Role.

postgresVocabularyGaps.$comment: NONE FOUND, and that is a measured answer rather than an omission. Every capability the currently-wired PostgreSQL runtimes actually resolve -- the Administration, Workforce, Commercial, CRM and Operations transports -- is already registered: employee.record.read, admin.principalAccess.read, admin.employeeProfile.write, customer.record.*, opportunity.*, salesAgreement.*, salesOrder.*, inventory.cycleCount.*. The unregistered ids all belong to functions that have NOT been cut over, which is DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER and not a registration omission. NO registration migration is proposed, because proposing one for a runtime that does not exist yet would be inventing authority.

equipment.$comment: The installed-asset register (eos_ops.equipment) has exactly ONE governed PostgreSQL writer: installSerializedUnitAsEquipment (functions/src/eosOps/equipmentCustody.ts:294), and it MOVES an existing AVAILABLE eos_ops.serialized_custody unit. Nothing in functions/src inserts a serialized_custody row -- serialized acquisition is still a Firestore path. So installed Equipment cannot be seeded without either inventing custody rows (a second authority) or connecting to Firebase (forbidden). The desired records are declared here so the scenario completes automatically once serialized acquisition lands in PostgreSQL.

parts.postgresAuthority: eos_ops.parts (migration 1759795200000 for the identity, 1759881600000 for the descriptive authority) IS the canonical PostgreSQL Part Master table, with NOT NULL internal_part_number, name, status, stocking_unit, control_type, stocking_class and the rest.
parts.governedWriter: functions/src/catalogMaster/postgresPartMasterWriter.ts EXISTS and is DELIBERATELY INACTIVE: catalogWriterState.ts declares CATALOG_WRITER_AUTHORITY = { firestore: OPEN, postgres: INACTIVE }, and the table is populated only by the explicit catalog cutover (copy -> verify -> reconcile -> cut over).
parts.$comment: BECAUSE a governed writer exists and is switched off, a direct insert here is NOT available: the direct-insert policy applies only where NO governed writer exists. Writing descriptive Part rows around an inactive writer would make this seed a second catalog authority and would collide with the cutover that owns the table. The Part records below are therefore declared fixture metadata, referenced by the purchasing, supplier-catalog and cycle-count rows (none of which has a foreign key to eos_ops.parts -- migration 026 says so explicitly), and written NOWHERE.

operatorLink.$comment: eos_ops.trucks carries no employee or technician column (migration 1758326400000), and there is no governed PostgreSQL Employee<->Technician relationship anywhere in functions/migrations. `desiredOperator` is scenario metadata ONLY and is written nowhere. The trucks and their mobile inventory locations ARE seeded independently, which is legitimate; the person-to-truck relationship is not invented.

inventory.balanceAuthority: DERIVED. On-hand is a sum over eos_ops.inventory_movements; no stored balance exists anywhere (warehouseBinRepository.ts:45).
inventory.$comment: The ONLY governed PostgreSQL writer of eos_ops.inventory_movements is cycleCountRepository.reconcileLine (functions/src/eosOps/cycleCountRepository.ts:325). Receiving does NOT post a movement in PostgreSQL. So every seeded on-hand quantity in this manifest arrives through an APPROVED cycle-count variance, which is an honest, governed, auditable adjustment -- not an invented opening balance.

openingBalances.$comment: There is no governed PostgreSQL writer for an opening/receipt balance movement. Rather than insert inventory_movements directly -- which would make this seed a second inventory authority -- opening stock is established through the cycle-count reconciliation path below, and anything that path cannot express is reported, not manufactured.

financialFixtures.$comment: NO ACCOUNTING DATA IS INVENTED. eos_commercial.invoices / invoice_lines / payments / payment_applications have governed writers (functions/src/eosOps/invoiceAuthority.ts, cashApplicationAuthority.ts), but an invoice is a CONSEQUENCE of priced Sales Order lines, and Sales Order LINES cannot be seeded: the commercial command layer refuses CATALOG_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE for any PART / EQUIPMENT_MODEL line reference (commercialCommandKernel.ts:110-116) because no PostgreSQL CommercialCatalogAuthority is composed. scenarios.name: RETAIL SALES LIFECYCLE
scenarios.narrative: Retail Sales A owns Retail Account A, its primary Contact and its main Location, and carries an Opportunity through an Agreement to a Sales Order. Retail Sales B runs a separate Account at a different pipeline stage.

scenarios.name: NATIONAL ACCOUNTS
scenarios.narrative: National Accounts Sales owns a National Account with three Contacts and three Locations, and carries it to an Agreement and a Sales Order. Distinct from retail by Job Role, Account segment and record set.

scenarios.name: CUSTOMER + EQUIPMENT
scenarios.narrative: Account -> Location -> installed Equipment -> Equipment Model.

scenarios.name: SERVICE
scenarios.narrative: Customer -> Location -> Equipment -> service need -> inbound work -> Work Order -> technician work -> parts usage -> completion.
scenarios.completesAutomaticallyWhen: A governed PostgreSQL Work Order authority exists AND EMP-RT-05 lands the governed Employee assignment authority. The desired chain is fully specified in `service.desired` so no new decision is needed then.

scenarios.name: PARTS / INVENTORY / PURCHASING
scenarios.narrative: Part -> supplier -> warehouse -> bin -> reorder need -> Parts Manager -> purchase order -> receipt. Parts Manager records purchase orders and voids one; the Parts Associate raises the request and books the receipt.

scenarios.name: WAREHOUSE / CYCLE COUNT
scenarios.narrative: Warehouse -> bins -> cycle count -> discrepancy -> reconciliation, with a genuine separation of duties between the counting Warehouse Associate and the reconciling Warehouse Manager. The approved variances are the ONLY governed on-hand movements this seed creates.

scenarios.name: EMPLOYEE LIFECYCLE
scenarios.narrative: Technician On Leave is ON_LEAVE with a preserved reporting relationship and NO user access and no new current work. Contract Technician is CONTRACTOR, holds legitimate contractor work in the desired service chain, and is accountability-ELIGIBLE under COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNTABILITY_ELIGIBILITY_V1 exactly as an ACTIVE employee is -- which is what makes CONTRACTOR distinct from ON_LEAVE rather than merely differently labelled.

scenarios.name: MANAGEMENT
scenarios.narrative: Managed Employees is non-vacuous at every level: Owner manages 1, General Manager manages 6, Service Manager manages 5, Parts Manager manages 2, Warehouse Manager manages 1, Office Manager manages 1. The General Manager is additionally the Accountable Person on three commercial records they do not own.

blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: createReceivingOrder (eosOps/purchasingRepository.ts:539) writes receiving_orders + receiving_order_lines ONLY. The sole governed PostgreSQL writer of eos_ops.inventory_movements is cycleCountRepository.reconcileLine. Posting a receipt movement here would make this seed a second inventory authority.

blockedRelationships.desired: warehouse HAS_OPENING_ON_HAND part
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: Same finding as above, stated for the opening-balance case. Opening stock in this seed is established through an APPROVED cycle-count variance instead, which is governed and auditable.

blockedRelationships.desired: employee OPERATES truck
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: eos_ops.trucks (migration 1758326400000) has no employee or technician column, and no governed PostgreSQL Employee<->Technician relationship exists. Trucks and their mobile inventory locations are seeded independently; the person relationship is not invented.

blockedRelationships.desired: opportunity/salesOrder HAS_LINE part / equipmentModel
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: commercialCommandKernel.ts:110-116 refuses CATALOG_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE for any PART / EQUIPMENT_MODEL line reference because no PostgreSQL CommercialCatalogAuthority is composed anywhere in functions/src. Commercial records are therefore seeded as headers with owner + accountable person and no lines.

blockedRelationships.desired: salesOrder BILLED_BY invoice; invoice SETTLED_BY payment
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: Consequence of COMMERCIAL_LINE_CATALOG_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE: an invoice without the priced lines it bills would be a manufactured number. The invoice and cash-application writers exist and are ready.

blockedRelationships.desired: reportDefinition OVER equipment / workOrder objects
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: Saved report definitions are Firestore-authoritative; the equipment and workOrder report objects have no seedable rows behind them here.

blockedRelationships.desired: employee HAS_DISABLED_USER_ACCESS
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: functions/src/adminPolicy/policyCommands.ts exposes createRole / assignRole / revokeRole and no principal-disable command. A DISABLED user-access state therefore cannot be established by a governed writer, so no persona in this manifest declares it; the two no-access personas declare NONE, which IS seedable (by seeding no Principal at all).

blockedRelationships.desired: employee HAS_JOB_ROLE jobRole
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: EMP-RT-08. eos_workforce.employees has no job role column (migrations 1759104000000 + 1759838400000). Job Role stays manifest metadata and is written nowhere.

blockedRelationships.desired: transferOrder MOVES part FROM warehouse TO warehouse
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: createTransferOrder (eosOps/purchasingRepository.ts:721) exists and is governed, but a transfer that changes on-hand needs the movement writer that INVENTORY_RECEIPT_MOVEMENT_BLOCKED records as absent. A transfer order with no balance effect would misrepresent the scenario, so it is declared and not seeded.

blockedRelationships.desired: persona HOLDS capability (for every capability the Role catalog declares)
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: eos_policy.capabilities is registered by migration and currently holds 37 keys, while functions/src/access/permissionCatalog.ts declares several hundred. Ids such as workOrder.create, workOrder.transition, inventory.balance.read, inventory.catalog.read, audit.event.read, finance.*, reorder.* and warehouse.transferOrder.read have NO PostgreSQL capability row, so no grant can exist for them and no verifier can resolve them. The sample company's access contract is expressed strictly in the registered vocabulary rather than asserting capabilities the authority cannot represent.

blockedRelationships.desired: some Role HOLDS workOrder.lifecycle.dispatch / .complete / .cancel, inventory.cycleCount.close, inventory.workOrderConsumption.record
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: These five ids ARE registered in eos_policy.capabilities but no Role in compatibilityRoles.ts or governedBusinessRoles.ts declares them, so the Role-catalog derivation grants them to nobody. They are asserted as FORBIDDEN where a persona might otherwise be assumed to hold them, which is why the Owner/Executive contract forbids workOrder.lifecycle.dispatch.

blockedRelationships.desired: part EXISTS in the PostgreSQL catalog with its name, status, control type and manufacturer
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: eos_ops.parts is the canonical PostgreSQL Part Master table and functions/src/catalogMaster/postgresPartMasterWriter.ts is its governed writer -- but catalogWriterState.ts CATALOG_WRITER_AUTHORITY declares postgres: INACTIVE, Firestore is still OPEN, and the table is filled only by the explicit catalog cutover. A governed writer that exists and is switched off is not an absent writer, so the direct-insert policy does not apply and this seed writes no Part row at all. The purchasing, supplier-catalog and cycle-count rows carry the declared part ids as unjoined governed keys (no foreign key references eos_ops.parts), so the operational chain still connects.

blockedRelationships.desired: technician HOLDS a governed PostgreSQL capability
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: See expectedAccess.accessFindings: DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER. Work Orders have no PostgreSQL table and the Reorder runtime is still the Firestore command path, so none of the technician Role's eight ids is registered in eos_policy.capabilities.

blockedRelationships.desired: service manager / dispatcher HOLDS work order lifecycle authority
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: See expectedAccess.accessFindings: DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER. The declared ids are unregistered and the registered workOrder.lifecycle.* ids are declared by no Role; the Work Order domain has not been cut over.

blockedRelationships.desired: parts manager HOLDS reorder.request.* / reorder.purchaseOrder.*
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: See expectedAccess.accessFindings: DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER. eosOpsHttp.ts serves only /operations/inventory with a read-only operation set, so no PostgreSQL runtime resolves a purchasing capability.

blockedRelationships.desired: warehouse manager HOLDS bin and transfer capabilities
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: See expectedAccess.accessFindings: DOMAIN_AUTHORITY_NOT_CUT_OVER. Same evidence; the warehouse repositories are governed writers with no request-time PostgreSQL authorization path.

blockedRelationships.desired: parts associate HOLDS conditioned reorder execution authority
blockedRelationships.missingAuthority: See expectedAccess.accessFindings: CONDITIONAL_AUTHORITY_GAP. eos_policy.role_capabilities has no condition column, so operationalRoleActive(PARTS_ASSOCIATE) cannot be represented and granting the ids would grant them unconditionally.

directInserts.why: NO governed Employee writer exists in the repository. Migration 1759104000000 built the Employee AUTHORITY, not a write path, and functions/src/access/employeeProfileCommands.ts is the FIRESTORE profile command. This is the same finding, and the same disposition, that functions/scripts/seedSyntheticNonprodWorkforce.js already records and that Owner ruling 2026-09-14 accepted.
directInserts.driftProtection: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then a full column-by-column comparison against the manifest. Any difference is FIXTURE_DRIFT and the run refuses. Profile columns are filled ADDITIVELY and only where the stored value IS NULL, so a v1-seeded Employee gains its profile without any value ever being overwritten.
directInserts.productionFence: The whole script refuses before `pg` is resolved unless the registry --environment is non-production by role AND by project id, EOS_ENVIRONMENT reads exactly `nonprod`, the environment is exactly `platform-sandbox`, and the Certification world is refused by id. Proved by subprocess in functions/test/operatorScriptEnvironmentFence.test.mjs.
directInserts.runtimeReuse: NONE. This SQL lives only in scripts/seedSampleCompany.js, which no application runtime path imports.

executionOrder: 1. environment + tenant validation (fence, then tenant resolved by key, never created)
2. administering Principal resolved and its own Role assignments read (the seed asserts no authority of its own)
3. capability / Role grant reconciliation (dry run first; eos_policy.role_capabilities)
4. Employees (eos_workforce.employees) -- every later Employee reference needs the row
5. Employee profile facts (additive fill of NULL profile columns on the same rows)
6. Principals + tenant memberships (ensureTenantPrincipal)
7. Employee <-> Principal links (establishLink; needs both the Employee and the Principal)
8. Security Role assignments (assignRole; needs the Principal)
9. Reporting relationships (establishReportingRelationship; needs BOTH Employees and the actor's admin.employeeProfile.write grant from step 3)
10. CRM Accounts (owner_employee_id -> Employees)
11. CRM Contacts and Locations (account_id -> Accounts; owner inherited in the create transaction)
12. Equipment models (eos_ops.equipment_models; no dependency)
13. Equipment (installed) -- BLOCKED, no write
14. Commercial records + governed accountable person (account_id -> Accounts, owner/accountable -> Employees, opportunity/agreement -> earlier records)
15. Part identities -- BLOCKED (the governed PostgreSQL Part Master writer is INACTIVE); no write
16. Suppliers, then supplier catalog items (part_id -> parts, supplier_id -> suppliers)
17. Warehouses, then bins (bins carry a composite FK to their warehouse)
18. Mobile locations, then trucks (a truck's mobile location link needs the location; home_warehouse_id needs the warehouse)
19. Purchasing: reorder request -> purchase order (needs the request in PURCHASING_IN_PROGRESS) -> receiving order / void (needs the purchase order)
20. Cycle counts: sheet -> line -> submit -> reconcile (reconcile posts the inventory movement, and is the last write)
21. Service / inbound work -- BLOCKED, no write
22. Derived reporting / financial consequences -- BLOCKED, no write
23. Verification (functions/scripts/verifySampleCompany.js)
$binRackingVocabulary_comment: eos_ops.bins constrains the racking in SQL: area ~ ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,31}$, aisle ~ ^[A-Z]{1,2}$ (LETTERS ONLY, one or two), bay 0-9999, position 0-99999 (migration 1758240000000). The values below satisfy those checks; a numeric aisle would be refused by the database.
$operationalNumberFormats_comment: eos_ops enforces the operational number formats in SQL: reorder requests ^RR-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6,}$ and receiving orders ^RO-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6,}$ (migration 1758672000000). The numbers below are in those formats; anything else is refused by the database rather than by this manifest.
$principals_comment: TWO PRINCIPALS PER INTERACTIVE PERSONA, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM ACTIVE. `fixturePrincipal` is the v1 `eos-synthetic-nonprod` Principal, which NO verifier recognizes and which therefore cannot sign in; `loginPrincipal` is the real `firebase`-provider Principal the deployed runtime actually resolves. The activate-logins phase ensures the sandbox Auth account, resolves the Principal from its uid, REVOKES the fixture link through the governed lifecycle and establishes the login link -- never two simultaneous active links for one Employee, which the partial unique index makes structurally impossible anyway.

sandboxCredentials.accountPolicy: ABSENT -> create a passwordless sandbox-only Auth account. EXISTING -> REUSE; never delete and never recreate to reseed. MATERIALLY INCONSISTENT (disabled, or an email that is not the manifest's) -> FIXTURE_DRIFT and refuse.
sandboxCredentials.passwordPolicy: THE SAMPLE COMPANY GENERATES NO SECRET OF ITS OWN. --mode activate-credentials DELEGATES to activateMissingSandboxPasswords in functions/scripts/activateSandboxPersonas.js -- the same function that script's own --activate-missing CLI calls -- narrowed by an explicit allowlist to this manifest's interactive personas. Its semantics are unchanged: a strong random password ONLY for a persona that has none, every working persona left untouched, merged into the gitignored credential file rather than replacing it, an unparseable file refused. --rotate is REFUSED by name in the orchestrator and is unreachable through any Sample Company path.
sandboxCredentials.activationCommand: node scripts/seedSampleCompany.js --environment platform-sandbox --databaseUrlEnv DATABASE_URL --tenantKey taylor-nonprod --existingAdminPrincipalId <principal id> --performedBy <operator> --mode activate-credentials --apply --firebaseProjectId eos-platform-sandbox --credentialFile <operator file ending credentials.local.json>
sandboxCredentials.delegatesTo: functions/scripts/activateSandboxPersonas.js activateMissingSandboxPasswords (one implementation, called by both its own CLI and this orchestrator; never copied)
sandboxCredentials.scope: EXACTLY the manifest Employees with sandboxPersona.interactiveLogin = true. The reused real Administrator is EXCLUDED -- its credential is real, pre-existing and out of scope, and its credentialEmail is null so it cannot become an allowlist entry. An @sandbox.invalid account outside the allowlist is never mutated; an allowlisted account that does not exist is REPORTED, never silently skipped.
